note: Tibshirani, Barber, Candes, Ramdas, 'Conformal Prediction Under Covariate Shift' (arXiv 1904.06019). Abstract has both quoted phrases: the likelihood ratio is assumed known, and it 'can be estimated accurately' from a large unlabelled set of test covariates. The guarantee assumes the ratio is known; estimating it is a practical approximation with no guarantee attached. The arXiv page names no venue; the paper is generally cited as NeurIPS 2019, which I did not check against the venue's own listing.

Mehrtens, Bucher, Brinker, 'Pitfalls of Conformal Predictions for Medical Image Classification' (arXiv 2506.18162, June 2025, labelled a preprint; the page links DOI 10.1007/978-3-031-44336-7_20, apparently a 2023 Springer proceedings version). The abstract says CP is unreliable under input and label shift, unreliable for subsets such as individual classes, and of limited value with few classes. The HTML has the CAMELYON17 sentence 'under domain-shift the coverage guarantee is not upheld' and says that re-calibrating on 1000 domain-shifted Camelyon17 images restores coverage. Caveats: the recalibration result is from one histopathology dataset only, and the 90% figure I found is an illustrative binary example, so I could not confirm 90% was the target in the Camelyon17 experiment.

Gibbs & Candes, 'Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Distribution Shift' (arXiv 2106.00170; arXiv lists no venue, widely cited as NeurIPS 2021). Abstract: shift is modelled as learning a single parameter that is re-estimated over time; the method 'provably achieves the desired coverage frequency over long-time intervals irrespective of the true data generating process'; it is robust on 2 real datasets with significant shift. The guarantee is long-run average coverage, not coverage at every time step.

Melki et al., 'Uncertainty Guarantees on Automated Precision Weeding using Conformal Prediction' (arXiv 2501.07185v1, preprint under review). The quotes are accurate: the 90% weed guarantee, 'the coverage guarantee is maintained for most of the farms' under near-OOD, and Farms 20 and 23 'far from the required 90% level'. But it is NOT a real deployment: it is an offline evaluation on an internal dataset of 510,600 images that simulates a near-OOD scenario, which the authors place between lab and real-world settings, with field testing left as future work. The formal 90% guarantee also applies only to the 'Weed in Set' decision rule. Correct to: 'In an offline, simulated near-OOD evaluation of a precision-weeding pipeline...'.

Core absence claim holds (best-effort): 2 quick searches found no conformal-prediction paper on crop disease image classification under lab-to-field shift. I also confirmed that the weeding paper's ref [18] is Domingues et al. 2022, Agriculture 12(9):1350, a general ML survey of crop disease and pest detection. Refuted because 'nearby agricultural work covers weeding, crop/weed and plant-species identification only' is wrong: Farag et al., 'Inductive Conformal Prediction for Harvest-Readiness Classification of Cauliflower Plants' (ICCV 2023 Workshops, CVPPA) is another agricultural CP image-classification paper. Drop the word 'only' or add harvest-readiness classification. Absence claims remain best-effort.
